prerequisites: While this course has no formal prerequisites, it is considered NECESSARY for proper utilization to have taken the first semester courses, especially those related to electricity and electronics.

learning_outcomes.text: Know and identify the different levels of the automation pyramid by studying the basic concepts, elements, functions, and techniques used in industrial automation and control systems.
Understand the properties and characteristics of the constituent elements of automatic systems in order to make a correct selection of them based on the system to be automated.
Be able to recognize the different types of signals and systems.
Understand and apply techniques and tools for the study and analysis of industrial automatic systems.
Understand the characteristics and differences of analog and digital control systems.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to automation and industrial control
Continuous Processes: Regulation and industrial control
Introduction to automatic control and regulation
Discrete Processes: Basic control systems and automation design
Design of Automatic Control Systems - GRAFCET
Types of sensors based on the variable to be measured

assessment_methods.method: Completion of practicals (exercises, cases, or problems)

assessment_rules: For continuous evaluation, the grade is based on a collective project report (30%), teamwork (10%), and a final exam (60%). A minimum grade of 4 in both the theory (40%) and exercise (60%) parts of the final exam is required for averaging. If continuous evaluation is renounced, the grade is based on a final exam (60%) and a practical lab test (40%), with a minimum of 5 required in the theory, exercise, and practical test components for averaging. Failure to attend the ordinary or extraordinary exam results in a 'Not Presented' grade. For the extraordinary call, students may keep positive continuous evaluation results; otherwise, 100% of the grade is obtained through a final evaluation similar to the renounced continuous evaluation path.
